metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Watford City, ND
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Watford City, ND, the McKenzie County seat and Bakken boomtown? Get an honest, well-informed offer on your interest.
heroLead: Watford City grew faster than almost any town in the country during the height of the Bakken boom, and the families who held onto mineral rights through that stretch watched their quiet ranch acreage turn into some of the most valuable ground in the state.
intro: The Long X Bridge, the man camps that came and mostly went, the housing prices that spiked and settled, all of it happened around mineral interests that in many cases had been sitting untouched since the original homestead. If your family is part of that story and you're now trying to figure out what your interest is actually worth today, past the boom-era headlines, that's exactly what we help with.

sections.heading: The McKenzie County seat, at the center of the core
paragraphs: Watford City sits in the thickest part of the Bakken and Three Forks fairway, and acreage around town has supported some of the highest-volume wells in the entire play. We check the specific spacing units and wellbores tied to your legal description, since even within this strong area, results vary tract to tract.

sections.heading: From boom-era leases to today's mature production
paragraphs: A lease signed in 2010 or 2011 during the height of the rush often looked very different from what's on the books now, with wells that have moved well past their peak production years. That's a normal part of the Bakken's lifecycle, and it's factored directly into how we value a Watford City-area interest today.

sections.heading: Families who watched the town change around their ranch
paragraphs: A lot of the people we talk to about Watford City minerals grew up watching cattle pasture turn into housing developments and truck stops almost overnight, then watched the pace slow again as the boom matured. That whiplash sometimes makes it hard to trust any number thrown out for a mineral interest, boom-era or otherwise.
We ground every Watford City offer in your actual well data and current production, not in memories of what the boom years looked like, so you're working with something real.

faqs.question: Our lease was signed during the height of the boom. Is it still in effect?
faqs.answer: Most boom-era leases here are held by continuous production, meaning they remain valid as long as a well keeps producing. We confirm your specific lease's status before making an offer.

faqs.question: How much has our well's production likely declined since the boom years?
faqs.answer: Significantly, in most cases, since Bakken wells lose a large share of their initial output within the first few years. We look at your actual recent statements to see where your well stands now.

faqs.question: Do you buy interests with multiple wellbores under one spacing unit?
faqs.answer: Yes, that's common around Watford City given the dense pad development here, and we account for all producing wells tied to your acreage.

faqs.question: Everything I remember about value here is from the boom years. Is that still accurate?
faqs.answer: Not usually. Wells have matured significantly since then, so we base any offer on current production and decline, not on what a similar interest might have fetched in 2011 or 2012.
